title: Migrating Rendering and Animations knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Migrating Rendering and Animations”?
options: Migrating Rendering and Animations helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Migrating Rendering and Animations means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Migrating Rendering and Animations removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Migrating Rendering and Animations should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Migrating Rendering and Animations helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Migrating Rendering and Animations is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Evaluating server-rendering changes” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Evaluating server-rendering changes” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Evaluating server-rendering changes” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Evaluating server-rendering changes” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Evaluating server-rendering changes” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Evaluating server-rendering changes” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Evaluating server-rendering changes” under Migrating Rendering and Animations. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Migrating Rendering and Animations”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
